newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-TAYLOR WRITTEN OFF AS "DEAD DUCK".
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TAYLOR WRITTEN OFF AS "DEAD DUCK".

text.p: Out-of-form captain Mark Taylor is becoming a luxury Australia cannot afford to carry in next week's first Ashes test against England, Australian newspapers decided on Wednesday.
"Dead Duck" said the headine in Sydney's Daily Telegraph after Taylor's latest setback on tour in England, a fourth-ball duck against against Gloucestershire.

"Given the Australians' collective poor form so far, there is a strong argument they cannot afford to carry anyone into the test who is so painfully unable to make a decent contribution, regardless of his status as captain," the paper said.
The Sydney Morning Herald agreed that Taylor, who has not scored a test 50 since late 1995 and scored only 18 in the firt two one-day matches against England, should go.
"On top of all that has preceded it (Taylor's latest failure), it is hard to argue that his place is sustainable any longer," the newspaper wrote.
England, who won the limited overs series 3-0 last weekend, host the tourists in the first test at Edgbaston from June 5, quickly followed by the second test at Lord's from June 19-23.
Taylors's immediate future rests with a three-man tour selection panel comprising coach Geoff Marsh, vice-captain Steve Waugh and Taylor himself.
"Unless Taylor can find any sort of form in the next week that (his place in the test team) should not be guaranteed," The Australian newspaper said.
"At the most he now has only the second innings of this game (against Gloucestershire) and a three-day match against Derbyshire, beginning on Saturday, to show something."
